exercises.prompt: You are given roster, an array of Pokémon records, each an object { name, type, attack } — for example { name: 'charmander', type: 'fire', attack: 52 }. Implement namesOfType(roster, type) so it returns an array of the names of every record whose type equals the given type, in the roster's original order. namesOfType(roster, 'fire') is ['charmander', 'vulpix', 'growlithe']. A type no record has, or an empty roster, returns an empty array.
exercises.fixture:
const roster = [
  { name: 'charmander', type: 'fire', attack: 52 },
  { name: 'squirtle', type: 'water', attack: 48 },
  { name: 'bulbasaur', type: 'grass', attack: 49 },
  { name: 'pikachu', type: 'electric', attack: 55 },
  { name: 'vulpix', type: 'fire', attack: 41 },
  { name: 'psyduck', type: 'water', attack: 52 },
  { name: 'oddish', type: 'grass', attack: 50 },
  { name: 'growlithe', type: 'fire', attack: 70 }
]
hints: Two steps: keep only the records of the right type, then pull the name out of each survivor.
filter narrows the records by a test on each one — p => p.type === type — and map turns each kept record into a single field.
return roster.filter(p => p.type === type).map(p => p.name) — filtering before mapping keeps the names in their original order.

exercises.prompt: You are given roster, an array of Pokémon records of shape { name, type, attack }. Implement strongest(roster) so it returns the name of the record with the highest attack. strongest(roster) is 'growlithe'. Assume the roster has at least one record and a single clear winner.
exercises.fixture:
const roster = [
  { name: 'charmander', type: 'fire', attack: 52 },
  { name: 'squirtle', type: 'water', attack: 48 },
  { name: 'bulbasaur', type: 'grass', attack: 49 },
  { name: 'pikachu', type: 'electric', attack: 55 },
  { name: 'vulpix', type: 'fire', attack: 41 },
  { name: 'psyduck', type: 'water', attack: 52 },
  { name: 'oddish', type: 'grass', attack: 50 },
  { name: 'growlithe', type: 'fire', attack: 70 }
]

tests.expr: strongest([{ name: 'a', type: 'x', attack: 5 }, { name: 'b', type: 'y', attack: 8 }])
strongest([{ name: 'a', type: 'x', attack: 8 }, { name: 'b', type: 'y', attack: 5 }])
strongest([{ name: 'lo', type: 'x', attack: 1 }, { name: 'hi', type: 'y', attack: 100 }, { name: 'mid', type: 'z', attack: 50 }])

hints: Fold the records down to the single best one by carrying the current leader as you go, then read its name at the end.
reduce with no initial value seeds the accumulator with the first record; each step keeps whichever of best and p has the larger attack.
return roster.reduce((best, p) => (p.attack > best.attack ? p : best)).name — compare on .attack while carrying the whole record, so .name is there when you finish.

exercises.prompt: You are given roster, an array of Pokémon records of shape { name, type, attack }. Implement countByType(roster) so it returns an object mapping each type to how many records have it — { type: count }. countByType(roster) is {fire: 3, water: 2, grass: 2, electric: 1}. An empty roster returns an empty object {}.
exercises.fixture:
const roster = [
  { name: 'charmander', type: 'fire', attack: 52 },
  { name: 'squirtle', type: 'water', attack: 48 },
  { name: 'bulbasaur', type: 'grass', attack: 49 },
  { name: 'pikachu', type: 'electric', attack: 55 },
  { name: 'vulpix', type: 'fire', attack: 41 },
  { name: 'psyduck', type: 'water', attack: 52 },
  { name: 'oddish', type: 'grass', attack: 50 },
  { name: 'growlithe', type: 'fire', attack: 70 }
]

tests.expr: countByType([{ name: 'a', type: 'fire', attack: 1 }, { name: 'b', type: 'fire', attack: 2 }])

hints: This is a frequency tally, but the value you count is each record's type field rather than the record itself.
Walk the records and bump the bucket for p.type: counts[p.type] = (counts[p.type] || 0) + 1.
Loop the roster updating counts[p.type] = (counts[p.type] || 0) + 1, then return counts — || 0 handles the first record of each type.

exercises.prompt: You are given roster, an array of Pokémon records of shape { name, type, attack }. Implement totalAttack(roster) so it returns the sum of the attack fields across all records. totalAttack(roster) is 417. An empty roster returns 0.
exercises.fixture:
const roster = [
  { name: 'charmander', type: 'fire', attack: 52 },
  { name: 'squirtle', type: 'water', attack: 48 },
  { name: 'bulbasaur', type: 'grass', attack: 49 },
  { name: 'pikachu', type: 'electric', attack: 55 },
  { name: 'vulpix', type: 'fire', attack: 41 },
  { name: 'psyduck', type: 'water', attack: 52 },
  { name: 'oddish', type: 'grass', attack: 50 },
  { name: 'growlithe', type: 'fire', attack: 70 }
]

tests.expr: totalAttack([{ name: 'a', type: 'x', attack: 5 }, { name: 'b', type: 'y', attack: 7 }])

hints: Fold the records into one running total, adding each record's attack rather than the record.
reduce with a 0 seed accumulates the sum: (sum, p) => sum + p.attack.
return roster.reduce((sum, p) => sum + p.attack, 0) — the 0 seed is both the starting total and the empty-roster answer.

exercises.prompt: You are given roster, an array of Pokémon records of shape { name, type, attack }. Implement strongestOfType(roster, type) so it returns the name of the highest-attack record among those whose type equals the given type — ignoring records of any other type. strongestOfType(roster, 'water') is 'psyduck'. Assume at least one record has the requested type.
exercises.fixture:
const roster = [
  { name: 'charmander', type: 'fire', attack: 52 },
  { name: 'squirtle', type: 'water', attack: 48 },
  { name: 'bulbasaur', type: 'grass', attack: 49 },
  { name: 'pikachu', type: 'electric', attack: 55 },
  { name: 'vulpix', type: 'fire', attack: 41 },
  { name: 'psyduck', type: 'water', attack: 52 },
  { name: 'oddish', type: 'grass', attack: 50 },
  { name: 'growlithe', type: 'fire', attack: 70 }
]

tests.expr: strongestOfType([{ name: 'a', type: 'fire', attack: 3 }, { name: 'b', type: 'water', attack: 9 }, { name: 'c', type: 'fire', attack: 7 }], 'fire')

hints: Narrow to just the records of the requested type first, so the global strongest of another type cannot sneak in.
After filter, fold the survivors to the biggest with the same running-best reduce, then read its .name.
roster.filter(p => p.type === type).reduce((best, p) => (p.attack > best.attack ? p : best)).name — the last test proves a stronger record of another type is correctly ignored.
